title: The inference speed of the int8 quantization version of SDXL is much slower than that of fp16
body:
The inference speed of the int 8 quantization version of SDXL is much slower than that of fp16. I am runing trt9.3 sdxl demo and here is the result. (I changed shape to 768x1344  manually)
fp16 : python3 demo_txt2img_xl.py "a photo of an astronaut riding a horse on mars" --version xl-1.0 --onnx-dir onnx-sdxl --engine-dir engine-sdxl --width 1344 --height 768
[I] Warming up ..
[I] Running StableDiffusionXL pipeline
|-----------------|--------------|
|     Module      |   Latency    |
|-----------------|--------------|
|      CLIP       |      2.45 ms |
|    UNet x 30    |   2616.81 ms |
|     VAE-Dec     |    222.92 ms |
|-----------------|--------------|
|    Pipeline     |   2851.01 ms |
|-----------------|--------------|
Throughput: 0.35 image/s

int8: python3 demo_txt2img_xl.py "a photo of an astronaut riding a horse on mars" --version xl-1.0 --onnx-dir onnx-sdxl --engine-dir engine-sdxl --int8 --quantization-level 3 --width 1344 --height 768
[I] Warming up ..
[I] Running StableDiffusionXL pipeline
|-----------------|--------------|
|     Module      |   Latency    |
|-----------------|--------------|
|      CLIP       |      2.39 ms |
|    UNet x 30    |   5550.13 ms |
|     VAE-Dec     |    223.70 ms |
|-----------------|--------------|
|    Pipeline     |   5785.81 ms |
|-----------------|--------------|
Throughput: 0.17 image/s

comments.author: nvpohanh
comments.body: Since INT8 MHA fusion for SeqLen>512 is not supported, adding Q/DQ before the FC after the MHA would cause an additional "Quantize" kernel which slows down the e2e perf. Therefore, the recommended quantization level for INT8 is 2.5

comments.author: akhilg-nv
comments.body:
@ecilay A100 should be working fine and has been tested on internally. Could you share more details about the OOM you're running into with SDXL? We're investigating such issues but it is unusual that you are experiencing this on 80GB A100. If you could share the details of the pipeline/options you are using, which step is running out of memory and error logs that would be helpful, as well as any relevant modifications you've made if any. You can also try using the `--build-static-batch` flag which has resolved some memory issues on devices with less memory. 

For TRT 10.0 installation, the readme steps are specific to the provided container which already contains TRT 8.6, which causes a quirk with the typical installation command when upgrading that requires installing twice and using `--force-reinstall` the second time. However, if you just do `python3 -m pip install --pre tensorrt` in your custom environment, this should work properly if an older TRT version is not already present.

If interested, you could also try follow readme in TensorRT Model Optimizer diffusers https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-Model-Optimizer/tree/main/diffusers to run SDXL int8 pipeline. It includes the environment setup instructions with docker.

comments.author: ckolluru
comments.body:
Can someone please elaborate on the ```UNet x 30``` module tested here? What does the ```x 30``` mean? 

Is it safe to assume that for a FP16 TensorRT optimized U-net model, the speed up one could possibly get by moving it to INT8 is around ```1.2 to 1.3x```? This seems to be a case of post-training quantization (PTQ), is the benefit with quantization aware training (QAT) only towards improved performance accuracy?

comments.author: akhilg-nv
comments.body:
x30 refers to the number of iterations of the U-Net used for denoising. The speed-up you see with Int8 quantization will ultimately depend on your hardware and model, but iirc 1.2-1.3x is a reasonable expectation on Ada GPUs for SDXL. The perf gains for PTQ/QAT should be the same if the same layers are being quantized, but QAT should theoretically improve the accuracy.

Closing this issue as there has been no further discussion on the original perf discussions for >3 weeks. If you have further questions closely coupled with the issue, feel free to continue here, otherwise we welcome you to start a new one with any additional follow-ups!
